instruction: Create a basic HAProxy load balancer config
output:
<think>
Goal: This is a straightforward network operations task that requires the right flags and arguments.

Plan: The right tool here is `cat` — cat command execution and management. `haproxy` will be used for TCP/HTTP load balancer. `systemctl` will be used for manage systemd services and units.

Precautions: SERVICE CONSIDERATION: Restart services during maintenance windows. Check unit dependencies beforehand with `systemctl list-dependencies`. After execution, validate that the system behaves as expected before closing the task.

cat > /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg << 'EOF'
global
    log /dev/log local0
    maxconn 4096
defaults
    log global
    mode http
    option httplog
    timeout connect 5000ms
    timeout client 50000ms
    timeout server 50000ms
frontend http-in
    bind *:80
    default_backend webservers
backend webservers
    balance roundrobin
    server web1 192.168.1.10:80 check
    server web2 192.168.1.11:80 check
EOF && systemctl restart haproxy
